title: Shift-out preserves concatenation
statement: Let $w$ assign a finite list of optional Boolean values to each of $\ell$ indices, and let the side word be the concatenation of these lists in index order. For any natural number $i$, shifting out leaves the side word unchanged: when $1\le i<\ell$, the list at index $i-1$ has length exactly $C_{i-1}=2\cdot 2^{i-1}$, and the list at index $i$ has room for $2^{i-1}$ more entries, the first $2^{i-1}$ entries of the list at $i-1$ are placed there, followed by the remainder of that list and the original list at $i$; in every other case the lists are unchanged.
